category_title: Students with EBD experiencing behavioral outbursts and academic difficulties in science
student_description: Sam is an 11-year-old who loves science but struggles with reading and core academic skills, leading to severe anxiety and outbursts when asked to read aloud or tackle unstructured tasks. He uniquely requires highly structured, reciprocal peer interactions and explicit visual/mnemonic scaffolds to bypass his reading insecurities and maintain behavioral regulation.

criteria.rationale: Sam's fear of peer judgment is mitigated when peer interactions are highly structured and he is given equal footing as both tutor and tutee.
criteria.check: The tutor's long-term plan includes regular, structured peer tutoring sessions (such as CWPT) where the student alternates between being the tutor and the tutee.

criteria.rationale: Because complex tasks trigger off-task behavior, Sam needs a sustained system to self-monitor his actions alongside his academic work.
criteria.check: The tutor incorporates explicit behavioral self-monitoring steps or checkpoints directly into the student's daily or weekly academic task checklists.
